judgements.reason: target covers marriage, property and assembly; slavery and the slave trade are never mentioned
no remedy or tribunal is mentioned, but the passage does say the family is 'entitled to protection by society and the State', which is adjacent to who must provide protection
no mention of penal offences, presumption of innocence or trials
freedom of movement and residence is absent; the only 'limitation' clause concerns race, nationality or religion in marriage, not movement
nothing about being denied a right to change anything; the word 'nationality' appears only as a prohibited limitation on marriage
no mention of elections, voting or suffrage
social security is never mentioned; 'society' appears only in relation to the family unit and its protection
no mention of work, remuneration or what pay must ensure
no mention of rest, leisure, working hours or holidays
no mention of a social or international order, nor of the Declaration's realization
no mention of States, groups or persons claiming a right to destroy rights
no four-item list of protected things; the passage does say 'No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property', which is adjacent to arbitrary interference
freedom of movement and residence and State borders are absent from the passage
no mention of government or the basis of its authority
no mention of remuneration or of what pay must ensure for a worker
motherhood and childhood are not mentioned, though the passage does say the family is 'entitled to protection by society and the State'
no mention of duties to the community or of development of personality
no mention of torture or of any treatment or punishment
no hearing, tribunal or trial appears; 'equal rights as to marriage' concerns marriage only
no mention of penal offences, acts or omissions, or national/international law
asylum, persecution and prosecutions are never mentioned
no mention of national effort, international co-operation, or how rights are realized
pay, work and discrimination in remuneration are absent; the passage's 'without any limitation' clause is about marriage
no right to security and no list of situations such as unemployment or sickness
the passage never states requirements that limitations must meet, but it does contain a limitation clause ('without any limitation due to race, nationality or religion')
the passage contains no interpretive clause about the Declaration as a whole
answered by 'No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property' -- property is the one thing the passage shields from arbitrary action, so a reader would answer 'property'
no mention of asylum, other countries or persecution
no mention of taking part in government, directly or through representatives
no mention of rest, leisure, working hours or paid holidays
no right to security and no circumstances such as disability, widowhood or old age
the passage never says limitations are determined by law, but it does mention limitations (due to race, nationality or religion) on marriage
no mention of recognition as a person before the law, nor of 'everywhere'
no hearing is mentioned, and no criminal charge or determination of rights and obligations
no mention of penalties or penal offences
the passage never speaks of dignity nor enumerates kinds of rights indispensable to it

the question is positional and self-contained: the target's first sentence is 'Men and women of full age ... have the right to marry and to found a family', so the last right listed is the right to found a family
motherhood and childhood and 'special care and assistance' are absent, though the passage does have an 'entitled to' clause about the family's protection
development of personality is not mentioned, but the passage calls the family 'the natural and fundamental group unit of society', which a reader might mistake for a setting claim
no mention of activities or acts aimed at destroying rights, nor any interpretive clause
